content:
If you're not in a rush to get your hands on the latest Apple product on launch day and are willing to wait a bit, Apple's official certified refurbished store has always been a reliable option. Generally speaking, about three months after a new product launches, the first batch of refurbished units will appear on Apple's website.

Other companies offer similar options, such as Amazon Renewed and Walmart Restored, but be aware that the standards and warranty terms they use are different⋯⋯

Apple Certified Refurbished Products

Buying from the Apple Certified Refurbished store usually saves you around 15%, and the product itself is completely identical to a brand-new one. Specifically, Apple promises all of the following:

  • Full inspection and testing performed by Apple
  • Brand-new exterior, so there won't be any scratches or scuffs
  • Brand-new battery, so battery life is the same as a brand-new unit
  • Comes with all original accessories and cables
  • Covered by Apple's standard one-year warranty, with the same coverage as a brand-new product
  • AppleCare+ can also be added

Basically the only difference you'll see is that the product comes in a plain white box rather than the original packaging.

Amazon Renewed

Amazon Renewed pricing is usually more competitive, but note that the product condition doesn't come with the same guarantees:

  • Inspection and testing performed by the seller rather than Apple
  • Used exterior, so there will be scratches and scuffs (see below)
  • Used battery, only guaranteed to still have at least 80% of its original capacity
  • Accessories may not be original Apple products
  • Comes with a 90-day Amazon warranty rather than Apple's one-year warranty

Regarding scratches and scuffs, Amazon offers three quality grades:

  • Premium / Excellent: No visible wear when viewed from 12 inches away
  • Good: Light scratches when viewed from 12 inches away, barely visible to the naked eye
  • Acceptable: Scratches easily seen and felt

Walmart Restored

Walmart Restored is even vaguer than Amazon — it doesn't spell out exactly what you're getting for your money:

  • No promises about cosmetic condition, only claims "performance and reliability like new"
  • No specifics on battery condition, only what was described above
  • No information provided about accessories
  • Warranty provided by the seller rather than Apple's one-year warranty

The Restored Premium tier comes with a one-year seller warranty, while the Like New, Good, and Fair tiers only get 90 days. The company doesn't clearly define what each tier actually represents.

9to5Mac's Take

If you want a product with both the appearance and Apple's warranty identical to a brand-new unit, the Apple Refurbished Store is clearly the top choice.

However, Amazon Renewed pricing can indeed be significantly cheaper, so if you're willing to accept the trade-offs listed above, it could be quite a good deal. Especially if you listen to us and save money by upgrading to the iPhone 17 Pro instead of this year's new model (just missing one feature), there are some pretty attractive deals here:

  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,214 (originally $1,599) — All-time low price
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,215 (originally $1,599) — All-time low price
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,208 (originally $1,599) — All-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,164 (originally $1,299) — All-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,170 (originally $1,299) — All-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,171 (originally $1,299) — Only $1 more than the all-time low

As for Walmart Restored, their promises are just too vague for me to feel comfortable, but if you're not satisfied, you can always opt for a return.
